extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, patent examiners, policy makers, and stakeholders concerned with patent examination process and RCE management
extracted.subtask_description: Audit-based standards and recommendations for managing Request for Continued Examination (RCE) backlog, examiner incentives, quality assurance, and outreach at the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office. Focuses on operational, policy, and quality-control criteria to reduce RCE pendency and minimize patent-term adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely determinations on RCEs (avoid patent-term adjustments)
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO must issue timely determinations on RCEs; statutory timeframes require actions (e.g., USPTO must provide a patent term adjustment when it takes the agency more than four months to issue an action subject to limitations). USPTO also has other statutory timing requirements (14 months for preliminary decision on new applications, 4 months for appeal responses, etc.) and provides an overall 3-year application pendency guarantee subject to limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delays in processing RCEs delay IP protection and can require USPTO to extend patent terms (patent term adjustment). The agency should monitor RCE pendency and take corrective action to meet statutory and internal timeliness metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigate structural and examiner-specific issues that increase RCEs
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate and address structural factors and examiner-specific behaviors that have increased the number of RCEs USPTO must act upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report recommends (a) researching reasons for variance in after-final amendment approval rates and the decline in after-final amendment filings; (b) assessing why applications handled by lower- and higher-grade examiners have different RCE filing rates; and (c) assessing reasons for variance among art units, identifying best practices that promote efficiency, and developing strategies to minimize patent term adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit introduction of new prior art in final rejections to permitted circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may include new prior art in final rejections only when permitted by policy (e.g., in response to amended claims or when cited in an information disclosure statement), consistent with MPEP 706.07(a) and 37 C.F.R. § 1.104(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants complained about new prior art in finals; the audit found examiners introduced new prior art only in response to amended claims as allowed. USPTO should ensure examiners follow MPEP and only cite new art when the amendment necessitates it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target quality assurance (OPQA) sampling to risk areas (e.g., actions with PTO-892/new prior art)
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA's statistical sampling of final rejections does not specifically target applications with indicators that new prior art was introduced (e.g., use of form PTO-892).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPQA can produce robust overall error estimates but is less likely to catch specific incorrect instances. The report recommends determining whether a stratified sample targeting applications with new prior art or other risk indicators would enhance QA and examiner-quality determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance production credit and docket management incentives between new applications and RCEs
rubrics_metrics.description: Production credit and docketing policies should not disproportionately incentivize examiners to work on new applications at the expense of RCEs. FY 2010 changes gave more credit for new applications and relaxed strict time requirements for RCEs, contributing to RCE backlog growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rebalance credits/docket rules (negotiated with POPA as needed) so examiners have appropriate incentives to process RCEs and new applications, avoiding the 'squeezing the balloon' effect where attention shifts away from RCEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a risk management plan for timely, situation-specific analysis and solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO should implement a documented risk management plan to ensure timely, situation-specific analysis and implementation of solutions to minimize patent-term adjustments when rebalancing resources is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation 3: the plan should enable prompt response to rapid RCE growth and document actions taken to meet statutory requirements and public expectations for prompt processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase participation in compact prosecution initiatives (AFCP 2.0, FAIP, QPIDS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs such as AFCP 2.0, FAIP, and QPIDS are intended to reduce likelihood of RCEs by resolving issues earlier in prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although participation was low, AFCP 2.0 lowered the likelihood of an RCE by ~20 percentage points and FAIP by ~7 points in analyses controlling for variables. USPTO should develop ways to increase participation and track effectiveness; recognize program limitations (e.g., time examiners have to consider after-final amendments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and address examiner grade effects on RCE filing rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications reviewed by lower-grade examiners (GS 9-11) were more likely to lead to RCEs than those reviewed by higher-grade examiners (GS 14-15).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO should assess whether differences reflect examiner experience/training or other factors and take corrective action where necessary (e.g., training, supervision, procedural adherence). The audit suggests ensuring new examiners follow standard procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop art-unit-specific RCE pendency targets and identify best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: RCE filing rates and pendency vary significantly by technology center and art unit (some art units >70% RCE filing rates; others under 40%; pendency from 107 to >300 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO should assess reasons for inter-art-unit variance, identify efficient practices, and set separate RCE pendency targets by art unit to better manage workload and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track and report program participation and outcomes consistently
rubrics_metrics.description: Accurate tracking of participation in initiatives (AFCP, FAIP, QPIDS) and their outcomes is necessary for assessing effectiveness; some early pilots lacked participant tracking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistent metrics and tracking (including baseline comparisons and time-bound outcome measures) so analyses of program impact on RCE likelihood are reliable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustain and diversify stakeholder outreach and communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage stakeholders (applicants, PPAC, public) through multiple channels (town halls, roadshows, social media, targeted communications) rather than relying solely on Federal Register notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outreach must be sustained to change applicant behavior and increase program participation; internal controls recommend adequate external communications to gather stakeholder input that affects agency goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research causes for decline in after-final amendment filings and approval rates
rubrics_metrics.description: After-final amendment filing rates and approvals declined substantially; after-final amendments are less costly to applicants ($0) and consume fewer examiner hours than RCEs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO should research why applicants file fewer after-final amendments and why approval rates changed, and address barriers (e.g., examiner willingness to enter after-final amendments, perceived likelihood of success) to encourage use of less-costly alternatives to RCEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure QA timing captures cases that become RCEs
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA performs checks on final rejections but does not necessarily time reviews to catch applications that will soon become RCEs; RCEs could be filed after OPQA checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QA processes should consider timing relative to applicant actions to better detect inappropriate introduction of new prior art and other errors that drive RCE filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use rigorous, data-driven analysis to assess RCE drivers and program effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ quantitative and qualitative methods (e.g., full-universe data 2004–2013, logistic regression controlling for technology center, examiner grade, and date; random samples of final rejections) to understand RCE trends and program impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The audit used these methods to detect drivers and program effects; USPTO should continue employing similar analyses for monitoring and policy development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce and deliver an action plan responding to audit recommendations within 60 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Per Department Administrative Order, USPTO must provide an action plan responding to the report's recommendations within 60 days of the memorandum date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency’s formal response was included in appendix D; timely submission of a documented action plan is required to implement recommended corrective actions.
